context.requirement_text:
Third and final part of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix, covering its own
explicitly-named SECONDARY surface: "Poller's per-tenant sweeps and
future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover
by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap." Atop
REQ-216's core module; does not touch REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring.

WHAT `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` ACTUALLY DOES TODAY (read in
full, not assumed): `handle_info(:tick, ...)` calls
`Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)
end)` -- SEQUENTIAL, one tenant schema at a time, not concurrent. The
same sequential pattern repeats for
`maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`,
`maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`,
`maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`. So THIS module does not exhibit
unbounded CONCURRENT demand the way the HTTP path does (each call
blocks the single Poller GenServer process, so at most one DB
connection is held by Poller work at any instant) -- the real gap
here is ACCOUNTING, not concurrency: Poller's one held connection is
invisible to REQ-216's admission budget, so REQ-216's global cap
(`pool_size - reserved_headroom`) can only be a safe ceiling on
HTTP-path concurrency if `reserved_headroom` already reserves enough
slack for Poller's own use -- an implicit, untested assumption today.
This requirement makes that assumption explicit and enforced rather
than merely documented.

SCOPE:
1. Before each of the six sequential per-tenant operations named
above (the timer poll-and-fire loop plus the five `maybe_run_*`
sweeps), acquire ONE global admission slot via
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)` for that operation's single
Repo-touching call, and release it immediately after that call
returns (success or the operation's own already-established rescue
path -- do not weaken any existing per-operation try/rescue
isolation boundary documented in poller.ex's moduledoc, e.g.
`maybe_run_alert_detection/3`'s own `rescue _ -> :ok`; the
acquire/release wraps around the existing isolation, it does not
replace it).
2. On `{:error, :capacity}` from `try_acquire(:global)` for a given
schema's operation within a tick: skip that one schema's operation
for that tick only (do not crash the GenServer, do not skip every
other schema's turn, do not skip that schema's OTHER operations this
tick if a later `try_acquire` call for a different operation
succeeds) -- mirroring `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`'s own existing
per-tick-degrades-gracefully philosophy already documented in this
module's moduledoc, applied per-schema-per-operation rather than
per-tick.
3. Poller does NOT use REQ-216's per-tenant semaphore -- only
`:global`. Reasoning: Poller's sweep already iterates every tenant
schema once per tick by design (REQ-186's own decision), so a
per-tenant CAP on Poller would not bound fairness between tenants the
way it does for bursty HTTP traffic, it would only cause a tenant to
be silently skipped some ticks for no client-visible reason -- a
strictly worse outcome for a background sweep whose whole contract is
"every tenant gets a turn." Stated explicitly rather than left
implicit.
4. No change to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree (no new
process; Poller remains the sole caller, same GenServer, same child
entry) and no change to `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own `poll_and_fire/1`
contract (unchanged input/output; the acquire/release wraps its call
site in `poller.ex`, per §1 above).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore or
REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring; no change to ISS-0430's future LISTEN/
NOTIFY work (named by ISS-0431 as a future secondary surface to cover
"by the same decision," not this requirement's own job to build); no
change to any `maybe_run_*` function's own internal per-schema
rescue logic beyond wrapping it in acquire/release.

task.description: REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2d) on REQ-218's implementation: idiom/scope/decision-record consistency, plus verification of ELIXIR-DEV's own flagged pre-existing gap.
acceptance_criteria: Verify with_admission/3's shape matches the validated design exactly (case/try/after structure, all 6 named operations wrapped consistently)
Verify the flagged pre-existing gap (fully-missing schema crashing poll_and_fire/1) is genuinely pre-existing and out of REQ-218's own scope
Verify AC3's antagonist-based test approach is a legitimate test-design choice, not a flaky test
Verify AC5's fault-injection approach is surgical and legitimate
Confirm no scope drift beyond poller.ex/test file/design doc/handoffs
Independently run mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force and mix format --check-formatted

result.diff_reviewed: git diff main..HEAD -- lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex (full diff read) and test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs (full file read); design doc lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md read in full; git diff main..HEAD --stat (whole repo) read to confirm scope.

idiomatic_vs_crutch.notes: with_admission/3 is a plain private helper, not a hand-rolled state machine standing in for gen_statem -- there is no state machine here to begin with (Poller is a GenServer ticking a stateless sweep, correctly modeled as such; REQ-186's own prior gate already settled that GenServer, not gen_statem, is the right shape for this module). The wrapper's control flow is exactly the design's own two-branch case on try_acquire(:global): {:ok, ref} -> try do fun.() after Admission.release(ref) end; {:error, :capacity} -> Logger.warning(...). All 6 named call sites (poll_and_fire, run_retention_sweep, build_context_and_detect, run_cycle, sweep_gaps, emit_lag_metrics) are wrapped with an identical with_admission(schema_name, op_atom, fn -> ... end) shape -- verified by reading each diff hunk. For rows 3-6, the existing rescue _ -> :ok is left INSIDE fun.(), unchanged, with the acquire/release wrapping around the whole try/rescue expression as a whole (not inside it, not replacing it) -- matches design §1 point 2 exactly. Release via `after` (not a plain post-call statement) is the correct idiom for guaranteed cleanup regardless of whether fun.() raises, matches Elixir's own try/after convention for resource release, and is NOT redundant with rows 3-6's own rescue since rows 1-2 have no inner rescue at all -- after is the only release mechanism for those two rows, exactly as the design's own rationale states.

supervision.notes: No new process, Task.start, spawn, or supervisor entry in this diff -- with_admission/3 is a plain function call executed inline on the Poller GenServer's own process, same as every operation it wraps. Letflow.Application's supervision tree is untouched (confirmed: lib/letflow/application.ex does not appear in git diff main..HEAD --stat). Poller remains the sole GenServer in lib/letflow/scheduler/ per the diff's own retained 'no second ticker' test. Letflow.Admission itself (the process being called into) is REQ-216's existing supervised singleton, unmodified by this diff -- lib/letflow/admission.ex does not appear in the diff stat either.

type_safety_gaps.verdict: NONE NEW, ONE PRE-EXISTING FINDING CONFIRMED (see below)
type_safety_gaps.notes: with_admission/3's own types are adequately guarded (@spec, is_function(fun, 0) guard, op as a plain atom label with no behavioral consequence per the design's own Q2). No new class of representable-but-invalid state is introduced by this diff. Separately, ELIXIR-DEV's own flagged finding -- Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 raising when a tenant's Postgres schema is entirely missing -- is a genuine contract violation (see verification below), but it is a pre-existing gap in Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1's own raise-safety guarantee, not a REQ-218 type-safety gap in the sense this REVIEWER role would fold into 'could a struct/Ecto.Enum make it unrepresentable' (it's a missing rescue boundary around a Repo call, not a missing type distinction). Recommending a follow-up issue for it below rather than filing it under the type-safety tag.

scope_creep.notes: git diff main..HEAD --stat -- lib/ shows exactly 2 files: lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md (new design doc) and lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex (the wiring itself) -- no drift into lib/letflow/scheduler.ex's own poll_and_fire/1 contract, lib/letflow/admission.ex's core semaphore, or lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex's HTTP-path wiring, matching REQ-218's own NOT-IN-SCOPE text. maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 (REQ-194) is confirmed left unwrapped in the diff -- matches the design's own §7 Q1 resolution (not one of the six named operations; ELIXIR-DEV did not silently extend coverage to a 7th operation 'for consistency', which the design explicitly forbade without a REVIEWER/requirement-text sign-off). No new behaviour, macro, or generic plugin/abstraction machinery was introduced -- with_admission/3 is a single private helper scoped to this one module, not a reusable framework piece built ahead of need.

result.pre_existing_gap_verification: Read Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 (lib/letflow/scheduler.ex:192-213) and its callee claim_due_timer_ids/2 (line ~219+): claim_due_timer_ids/2 runs a raw Ecto query against the tenant-schema-prefixed `timers` table with no try/rescue anywhere in its body or in poll_and_fire/1's own body. Confirmed poller.ex's own moduledoc (line 32) explicitly asserts poll_and_fire/1 'already guarantees it never raises' -- a documented contract this function does not actually meet for a tenant schema whose Postgres schema was never created (or was dropped) entirely: a Postgrex undefined_table/undefined_schema error propagates unrescued. This is independent of REQ-218's own change: REQ-218 wraps the CALL SITE in poller.ex (with_admission around Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)) but adds no rescue to poll_and_fire/1's own body, and could not have introduced this raise path since it never touches lib/letflow/scheduler.ex (confirmed via the diff stat above). ELIXIR-DEV's own account of discovering this via an early, since-abandoned AC5 test draft (a ghost schema with no CREATE SCHEMA at all) is corroborated by the current AC5 test's own deliberate avoidance of that exact fault shape (see test comment at poller_test.exs:459-474, which explains dropping only effect_completions rather than the whole schema for exactly this reason). Verdict: genuinely pre-existing, genuinely out of REQ-218's scope, correctly not fixed here.
result.follow_up_issue_recommendation: YES -- file a follow-up issue, following the ISS-0437 pattern (discovered_by: REVIEWER carrying forward ELIXIR-DEV's own finding, discovered_in_run: WF02-REQ218-20260903, severity: MINOR, tags: [scheduler, raise-safety, s6]). Title suggestion: 'Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1's documented never-raises contract does not hold for a tenant schema missing its Postgres schema entirely'. affected_files: lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex (moduledoc's contract claim). related: REQ-218, REQ-186. Recommend ORCH register this at Step Final (this REVIEWER does not create docs/issues/ entries itself). Rationale for filing rather than leaving as a local note: an unusual-but-not-impossible tenant state (mid-deprovisioning, per ELIXIR-DEV's own note) can currently crash the whole Poller tick's timer-poll pass for every schema in that tick (Enum.each has no per-schema rescue at that call site either, only REQ-218's admission wrapper which does not add a rescue) -- worth tracking as claimable work per core-directives.md's No-Issue-Left-Local-Only rule, not just recorded in this handoff's prose.

ac3_test_judgment.notes: AC3 requires demonstrating a genuine partial (not total) skip within one tick, which structurally requires a real concurrent contender racing for the sole global admission unit -- Poller itself is single-threaded/sequential (confirmed in §3 of the design and by poller.ex's own Enum.each shape), so it can never contend with itself. The antagonist Task (ac3_antagonist_loop/0) continuously acquires-then-releases the sole unit in a tight loop for the duration of one tick over 10 schemas, and the test retries up to 5 times, halting early on the first observed genuine mixed outcome (fired_count > 0 and < 10). This is a legitimate design for testing a race condition: (1) it tests the real production code path (real Letflow.Admission GenServer, real try_acquire/release calls), not a mock; (2) the retry loop only guards against WHICH schemas land on which side of the race, not whether a partial skip is possible at all -- with cap=1 and a tight-looping antagonist against 10 candidate acquisitions, the probability of either extreme (0 collisions or 10/10 collisions) across a full tick is low, and 5 attempts is a reasonable bound for a CI-safe nondeterministic race test (each attempt takes on the order of a full tick's DB round-trips across 10 schemas, not a tight spin, so the suite cost is bounded and the test fails loudly and honestly if all 5 attempts miss, rather than silently passing on a vacuous case). Independently re-ran the whole poller_test.exs suite 3 times in the foreground (see below) -- AC3's test passed cleanly every time, including with a fixed --seed, corroborating ELIXIR-DEV's own claim of having run it several times standalone. This is judged a legitimate test-design choice for a genuinely nondeterministic property, not a flaky test -- flagging for TEST-DESIGNER to keep an eye on if CI ever shows an intermittent failure needing a 6th retry or a different harness, but not a blocker.

ac5_test_judgment.notes: AC5 drops only the effect_completions table (via DROP TABLE ... CASCADE) from an otherwise fully-provisioned, fully-migrated tenant schema, rather than omitting the whole Postgres schema. This isolates the fault to exactly the three ordering rows (maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1, _sweeper/1, _metrics/1), all of which query effect_completions and share the same rescue _ -> :ok shape, while leaving poll_and_fire/1's own timers table, retention's tables, and REQ-194's active-instance refresh untouched -- avoiding the pre-existing poll_and_fire/1 gap entirely (verified above) rather than accidentally re-exercising it. The test additionally asserts a DIFFERENT (intact) schema's own timer still fires in the same tick (proving the broken schema's raise doesn't poison the whole tick) and that a post-tick try_acquire(:global) still succeeds under global_cap == 1 (proving no leaked ref) -- both are the correct assertions for what AC5 actually requires (rescue still catches, no leak, tick completes). This is a legitimate, narrowly-targeted fault injection, not over-reaching into the pre-existing gap.
